newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE volume reaches highest ever for November.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE volume reaches highest ever for November.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) said on Tuesday it traded its busiest November ever, trading a record 15.7 million contracts last month.

The volume was up 39 percent on November 1995 and November 1994. Average daily volume amounted to 745,602 futures and options contracts, representing an average daily nominal turnover of 166.11 billion stg, LIFFE said in a statement.
"I am pleased to see that LIFFE has already achieved a record trading year in the run up to Economic and Monetary Union (EMU)," said Daniel Hodson, chief executive of LIFFE.
The exchange said cumulative volume in 1996 to date has totalled 156.7 million contracts, beating the total annual 1994 volume of 153.0 million and 1995's volume of 132.7 million contracts.
LIFFE said its new one-month Euromark futures contract, launched on November 21, has averaged 2,578 contracts on a daily basis.

The FTSE 100 American style index option set a new daily record of 94,946 on November 5, beating the previous record of 57,736 set in August. The option also set a new monthly record of 429,818 contracts, beating the February 1994 record of 426,260.
End of month open interest settled at 6.2 million contracts.
